title: Approach: how films are made and checked | Plainsight Medical
desc: How a patient-education film is made: sourced script, clinician review and sign-off, production, preview and delivery. Plus what AI is and is not used for.

sections.text:
HOME
/
APPROACH
MADE QUICKLY. CHECKED slowly.
The films are produced with AI tools, which is why they are practical for a single consultant. The clinical content is controlled by a clinician, which is why they can be trusted.

STEP 01
KICK-OFF
We agree the topics as one batch, who will review scripts, who gives final approval, and your logo and colours. For a film with an AI presenter, the clinician signs a consent form and completes a short recording session.
STEP 02
SCRIPT
We draft each script from current NHS, NICE and specialist sources and list them. The script is written in plain English with UK wording, including when to call a GP, NHS 111 or 999.
STEP 03
YOUR REVIEW
Your reviewer sends one consolidated round of comments. We revise, and you sign off the script. Nothing is produced before that.
STEP 04
PRODUCTION
We build the anatomy, the patient scenes, the narration or AI presenter, captions and music.
STEP 05
PREVIEW
You receive a watermarked preview. Changes come back as one list.
STEP 06
SIGN-OFF
The approving clinician signs off the final film.
STEP 07
DELIVERY
You receive the finished files: the 16:9 master and, if ordered, the vertical version and shorts.

WHAT AI DOES, AND DOES NOT
THE TOOLS DRAW. A PERSON DECIDES WHAT IS true.
AI generates the imagery, the motion and the narration voice. It does not decide what the film says, and it does not get the last look.
FROM THE REVIEW LOG OF ONE FILM
A clot drawn bulging out through the artery wall.
Rejected. Three new versions made, one chosen.
A paramedic ECG with four electrodes, and the patient’s jumper had changed.
Rejected and redone.
Monitors in the catheter lab that switched to an invented X-ray after four seconds.
Shot cut before the change.
Pieces of plaque sliding along with the balloon.
Rebuilt so only the device moves along the wire.
Generated pictures can look right and be wrong. Every shot is reviewed against the script before it goes into a film, and the film is reviewed again by you.

SAFEGUARDS
SIX RULES EVERY FILM follows.
01
Sources are named
Every script lists the guidance it was drafted from. Figures we cannot source are left out rather than estimated.
02
You approve twice
Once at script, once at final film. Clinical content and claims stay under your control.
03
Emergency wording follows the NHS
When to call 999, NHS 111 or a GP is taken from NHS guidance, not paraphrased loosely.
04
No promises about outcomes
Films explain what happens. They do not claim one technique or surgeon is better than another.
05
No patient data
People in the films are AI-generated. No real patient is filmed, and no patient information is used.
06
Consent for likeness
An AI clone of a clinician is made only with signed consent, used only for that client’s approved films, and deleted on request.
